records.identifying_characteristics: Evergreen tree with curved, leathery leaf-like phyllodes bearing several parallel veins, pale yellow flower spikes and twisted pods.
records.typical_habitat: Disturbed open ground, roadsides, plantations and coastal sites in warm tropical areas.
records.documented_impacts: It can naturalise into dense stands that shade and displace native vegetation in invaded habitats.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the leaves, bark and pods without disturbing the plant; record the location and report it. Do not cut or remove it without site permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Fast-growing evergreen tree with large curved phyllodes, pale flower spikes and coiled dark pods containing black seeds with an orange aril.
records.typical_habitat: Humid tropical lowlands, plantations, roadsides and other open or disturbed land.
records.documented_impacts: Outside cultivation it can form persistent stands, alter open habitat and compete with native regeneration.
safe_response_guidance: Record bark, phyllodes and pods from a safe position and report the mapped point. Tree work or seed handling requires the land manager's permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Low creeping perennial legume with stolons, leaves divided into four oval leaflets, yellow pea-shaped flowers and fruit that develops below ground.
records.typical_habitat: Moist tropical lawns, slopes, orchards, plantations and managed pasture where it is used as ground cover.
records.documented_impacts: It spreads and persists as a dense planted ground cover; the reviewed source does not provide a formal species-specific environmental severity rating.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph flowers, four-part leaves and runners, then report the location. Because it may be deliberately planted, do not remove it without explicit permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Upright herb with narrow opposite leaves, red-and-orange flower clusters and long pods; broken tissue releases milky sap.
records.typical_habitat: Gardens, roadsides, waste ground and other sunny disturbed sites, including cultivated plantings.
records.documented_impacts: It can self-seed beyond cultivation; milky sap can irritate skin and eyes and plant tissues are toxic if eaten.
safe_response_guidance: Avoid sap contact and do not open pods. Photograph the flowers and leaves, record the location and obtain permission before any handling.

records.identifying_characteristics: Short-lived branching herb with opposite divided leaves, small white-and-yellow flower heads and narrow black seeds tipped with barbs.
records.typical_habitat: Road verges, gardens, cultivated fields, trail edges and other sunny disturbed ground.
records.documented_impacts: It competes as a fast-seeding weed, while barbed seeds spread readily on clothing, equipment and animal fur.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph before touching it and avoid carrying barbed seed. Report the location; only remove an authorised small plant before seed forms.

records.identifying_characteristics: Hairy creeping or twining legume with three broad leaflets, small bluish-purple pea flowers and flattened hairy pods.
records.typical_habitat: Plantations, forest margins, roadsides, riverbanks, pastures and other humid disturbed sites.
records.documented_impacts: Vigorous growth can form dense mats over shrubs and young trees, suppressing vegetation beneath it.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph leaves, flowers and pods without pulling vines through surrounding plants. Record and report the location, and wait for site authorisation.

records.identifying_characteristics: Fast-growing tree with ring-scarred hollow stems and very large, deeply palm-lobed leaves that are pale or whitish beneath.
records.typical_habitat: Forest gaps, riverbanks, roadsides, cleared land and other wet tropical disturbed habitat.
records.documented_impacts: It colonises gaps rapidly and can develop dense stands that shade native pioneer plants and alter regeneration.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph leaf shape, trunk scars and fruit from safe ground. Do not fell or prune the tree; report it to the responsible land manager.

records.identifying_characteristics: Branching shrub with opposite triangular leaves, three prominent veins from the leaf base and clusters of pale flower heads.
records.typical_habitat: Roadsides, plantation margins, grassland, forest edges and other open disturbed sites.
records.documented_impacts: It forms dense stands that suppress other vegetation; abundant wind-dispersed seed and regrowth from cut material aid spread.
safe_response_guidance: Do not cut a flowering or seeding stand. Photograph it, record the point and report it; remove only under an authorised site plan.

records.identifying_characteristics: Low branching herb with three-part leaves, small violet-purple flowers and long narrow capsules held on slender stalks.
records.typical_habitat: Gardens, lawns, roadsides, paths and other moist or shaded disturbed ground.
records.documented_impacts: It spreads as a weed of disturbed ground; the reviewed government source does not assign a formal environmental severity rating.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the three-part leaves, flowers and capsules and submit a location report. Do not weed it from land you do not manage.

records.identifying_characteristics: Fine creeping grass with stolons and rhizomes, narrow grey-green blades and three to seven slender seed spikes radiating like fingers.
records.typical_habitat: Lawns, roadsides, cropland, river margins and heavily disturbed or compacted open ground.
records.documented_impacts: Its dense mats compete strongly with crops and other low vegetation, and fragments of stolons or rhizomes readily re-establish.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph runners and seed heads and report the patch. Do not spread cut runners or soil, and only control it with the land manager's approval.

records.identifying_characteristics: Perennial sedge with solid triangular stems, narrow basal leaves, reddish-purple flower clusters and chains of underground tubers.
records.typical_habitat: Cultivated fields, gardens, lawns, roadsides and seasonally moist disturbed soils.
records.documented_impacts: It is a highly competitive crop weed; persistent tubers and rhizomes make disturbed infestations difficult to contain.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph stems and flower clusters and record the patch. Do not move contaminated soil or attempt removal without an approved plan for the tubers.

records.identifying_characteristics: Free-floating aquatic plant with glossy rounded leaves, often swollen leaf stalks, dangling dark roots and spikes of lavender flowers.
records.typical_habitat: Still or slow-moving freshwater, including ponds, lakes, drains, wetlands and quiet river margins.
records.documented_impacts: Rapidly expanding mats obstruct water movement and access, shade submerged life and reduce dissolved oxygen.
safe_response_guidance: Stay on stable ground, photograph the mat and record the location. Never enter water or return fragments to it; report the infestation for authorised control.

records.identifying_characteristics: Tufted annual grass with flattened whitish stem bases and several finger-like seed spikes whose spikelets line one side.
records.typical_habitat: Compacted paths, roadsides, lawns, plantations, gardens and cultivated fields.
records.documented_impacts: It is a prolific competitive weed of crops and disturbed ground, producing seed that persists and moves with soil and equipment.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the flattened base and seed spikes and report the patch. Avoid transporting seeding material or contaminated soil; obtain permission before control.

records.identifying_characteristics: Soft upright succulent herb with narrow serrated leaves, showy pink, red, purple or white flowers and explosive seed capsules.
records.typical_habitat: Cultivated gardens and moist disturbed ground in warm climates, sometimes persisting outside plantings.
records.documented_impacts: It can self-seed and escape cultivation; the reviewed regional profile does not establish a formal species-specific environmental severity rating.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph flowers, leaves and capsules and report the location. Because it may be cultivated and capsules disperse seed explosively, do not remove it without permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Fast-growing shrub or small tree with twice-divided leaves, cream spherical flower heads and clusters of flat brown pods.
records.typical_habitat: Roadsides, pastures, coastal areas, forest edges and other open disturbed land.
records.documented_impacts: It forms dense thickets, competes with native vegetation and maintains a persistent soil seed bank.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph foliage, flowers and pods and report it. Do not cut mature plants or move pods; authorised control must account for resprouting and seed.

records.identifying_characteristics: Emergent aquatic herb with upright oval leaves on three-angled stalks, pale yellow three-petalled flowers and rounded clusters of fruit.
records.typical_habitat: Shallow freshwater wetlands, swamps, drains, irrigation channels and rice-growing areas.
records.documented_impacts: Dense growth obstructs irrigation and drainage, competes in rice fields and displaces other aquatic vegetation.
safe_response_guidance: Observe and photograph from stable ground, record the waterbody and report it. Do not enter water or move plants, mud or fragments between sites.

records.identifying_characteristics: Tall clump-forming grass with broad blades, a conspicuous hairy collar and a large open, branching seed head.
records.typical_habitat: Road verges, pasture, plantation edges, disturbed woodland and other open sunny sites.
records.documented_impacts: Dense stands suppress native plants and create a heavy dry fuel load that can increase fire intensity and frequency.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the clump and open seed head and report the extent. Avoid moving seed or cutting dry stands; any control requires site authorisation and fire awareness.

records.identifying_characteristics: Fast-growing twining vine with opposite heart-shaped leaves, slender ribbed stems and clusters of small white flower heads.
records.typical_habitat: Plantations, forest edges, riverbanks, roadsides and moist disturbed vegetation.
records.documented_impacts: It rapidly blankets shrubs and young trees, suppressing growth; wind-borne seed and rooting stem fragments accelerate spread.
safe_response_guidance: Do not pull vines through vegetation or leave stem fragments on moist soil. Photograph, map and report the patch for authorised management.

records.identifying_characteristics: Scrambling shrub with sensitive twice-divided leaves, pink flower balls and strongly hooked prickles along its angled stems.
records.typical_habitat: Pasture, roadsides, plantation margins, stream edges and other humid disturbed ground.
records.documented_impacts: It forms prickly impenetrable thickets that exclude vegetation and livestock; long-lived seed spreads in soil, water and on equipment.
safe_response_guidance: Keep clear of hooked prickles, photograph from the path and report the patch. Do not enter, pull or transport it without trained authorised support.

records.identifying_characteristics: Large shrub with sensitive twice-divided leaves, pink flower balls, segmented hairy pods and stout thorns on stems and branches.
records.typical_habitat: Floodplains, wetlands, riverbanks, drains and seasonally wet disturbed land.
records.documented_impacts: It creates dense thorny wetland thickets that replace native vegetation, obstruct access and spread seed in floodwater and mud.
safe_response_guidance: Remain on stable access, photograph from a distance and report it. Never enter a thicket or water, and do not handle pods or move contaminated mud.

records.identifying_characteristics: Low creeping herb with reddish rooting stems, leaves of three heart-shaped leaflets, small yellow flowers and narrow seed capsules.
records.typical_habitat: Lawns, gardens, paths, nursery pots and moist disturbed soil.
records.documented_impacts: It is a persistent garden and turf weed whose capsules eject seed and whose rooting stems help patches spread; no formal severity rating is supplied here.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the three leaflets and yellow flowers and record the location. Treat this entry as information only and do not infer removal permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Upright branching herb with deeply divided leaves, many small white flower heads and ribbed dark seeds.
records.typical_habitat: Roadsides, pasture, cultivated land, drainage lines and other open disturbed ground.
records.documented_impacts: It competes strongly with crops and pasture and can cause dermatitis, hay fever and respiratory reactions in exposed people.
safe_response_guidance: Keep a safe distance, avoid touching or smelling the plant, photograph it and report the exact point. No beginner active removal is provided.

records.identifying_characteristics: Creeping salt-tolerant grass with rooting stolons and rhizomes, narrow leaves and usually two slender seed spikes at the stem tip.
records.typical_habitat: Saltmarsh margins, coastal dunes, estuaries, saline drains and irrigated turf.
records.documented_impacts: It can form dense mats in saltmarsh and other coastal habitat, displacing lower native vegetation and changing plant-community structure.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph runners, leaves and paired seed spikes and report the mapped patch. Do not move turf or fragments and obtain site permission before control.

records.identifying_characteristics: Tall perennial bunch grass with flat rough-edged leaves and conspicuous yellowish to brown bristly cylindrical flower heads.
records.typical_habitat: Roadsides, pasture, savanna, open woodland and disturbed tropical grassland.
records.documented_impacts: Dense stands displace native grasses and add substantial dry fuel, promoting hotter and more frequent fires.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the whole clump and bristly seed head and report its extent. Do not cut or carry seeding plants; control needs authorisation and fire-risk planning.

records.identifying_characteristics: Shrub or small tree with smooth peeling bark, opposite strongly veined leaves, white flowers and round edible yellow fruit.
records.typical_habitat: Forest edges, pasture, disturbed woodland, roadsides and abandoned cultivated land.
records.documented_impacts: It forms thickets that compete with native vegetation; birds and mammals disperse fruit seed and cut stems may resprout or sucker.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph bark, leaves and fruit and report the location. Do not cut established trees or move ripe fruit; obtain land-manager approval.

records.identifying_characteristics: Robust tall annual grass with brace roots near the base, broad leaves bearing irritating hairs and a thick cylindrical jointed seed head.
records.typical_habitat: Cropland, plantation rows, roadsides, ditches and other moist disturbed tropical sites.
records.documented_impacts: It is a serious competitive crop weed; rapid growth and abundant seed reduce yields, while stiff hairs can irritate skin.
safe_response_guidance: Avoid skin contact, photograph the base, leaves and seed head and report the patch. Do not move seed-bearing material or remove it without authorisation.

records.identifying_characteristics: Low branching herb with opposite wrinkled leaves, small purple flowers and distinctive overlapping green bracts resembling a shrimp spike.
records.typical_habitat: Shaded moist gardens, forest margins, paths and other disturbed tropical sites.
records.documented_impacts: It can become locally abundant and spread by seed, but the reviewed risk assessment considered significant environmental impact unlikely.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the bracts, flowers and leaf texture and report the location. Do not remove a garden or wild plant without the responsible manager's permission.

records.identifying_characteristics: Free-floating fern with paired folded oval leaves covered in water-repellent hairs and a submerged root-like third leaf; it has no flowers.
records.typical_habitat: Still and slow-flowing freshwater such as ponds, lakes, wetlands, drains and sheltered river margins.
records.documented_impacts: Thick floating mats block light and oxygen, degrade aquatic habitat and obstruct irrigation, navigation and water access.
safe_response_guidance: Stay out of the water, photograph the leaf hairs and mat and report the waterbody. Do not move or break plants because small fragments can spread.

records.identifying_characteristics: Tough upright herb or small shrub with narrow toothed leaves, small yellow flowers and dry fruit segments bearing catching awns.
records.typical_habitat: Pasture, roadsides, waste ground, field margins and other open disturbed sites.
records.documented_impacts: It competes in pasture and disturbed vegetation; awned fruit segments spread on fur, clothing, vehicles, equipment and contaminated material.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph leaves, flowers and fruit and inspect clothing for caught segments. Report it and do not remove woody or seeding plants without authorisation.

records.identifying_characteristics: Small erect parasitic herb with narrow leaves and bright red, orange, pink or yellow tubular flowers emerging close to host grasses or crops.
records.typical_habitat: Fields and disturbed grassland where susceptible cereals or other grass hosts grow.
records.documented_impacts: Its roots attach to host roots and steal water and nutrients, causing severe stunting and yield loss in cereal crops.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the flower and host crop without pulling it, mark the exact point and report it promptly. Do not move soil or seed from the site.

records.identifying_characteristics: Branching annual herb with opposite toothed leaves and small yellow flower heads clustered on short stalks in the leaf axils.
records.typical_habitat: Gardens, plantations, roadsides, paths, waste ground and other moist disturbed places.
records.documented_impacts: It can form thick weed growth in disturbed sites and compete with low vegetation; the reviewed source does not provide a formal severity rating.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph the opposite leaves and axillary flower heads and report the location. Avoid moving mature seed and obtain permission before weeding.

records.identifying_characteristics: Robust sprawling grass with long stolons that root at nodes, broad hairy leaves and an open branched flower head.
records.typical_habitat: Wetlands, drains, riverbanks, floodplains and other seasonally or permanently wet disturbed ground.
records.documented_impacts: It forms dense mats that replace native wetland plants, obstruct water movement and create additional dry-season fire fuel.
safe_response_guidance: Photograph rooted runners and the flower head from stable ground and report the extent. Do not enter wetlands or move fragments; control requires authorisation.
